sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时所经历的重大人生变化与转型的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些变化对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们将继续剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Anxiety feels like such a curse.
sentences.zh: 焦虑感觉就像是一种诅咒。

sentences.en: I'm just going to come out and say it.
sentences.zh: 我只想直截了当地说出来。

sentences.en: I think a lot of us have probably wished for a day where we weren't anxious just one day.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人可能都曾希望过，哪怕只有一天，能过上没有焦虑的日子。

sentences.en: What might that be like?
sentences.zh: 那会是什么样子呢？

sentences.en: Or we've considered, you know, what our lives would look like if we weren't held back by these hypothetical fears about what may or may not happen, what others might think,
sentences.zh: 或者我们曾想过，如果我们没有被那些关于可能发生或不会发生的事情、关于别人会怎么想的假设性恐惧所束缚，我们的生活会是什么样，

sentences.en: what disasters await, what terrible things could go wrong in our future.
sentences.zh: 那些等待着我们的灾难，以及未来可能发生的糟糕事情。

sentences.en: It is a huge burden at times.
sentences.zh: 这有时是一个巨大的负担。

sentences.en: Even if it comes and goes in waves, me and my anxiety, my pal, we go way back.
sentences.zh: 即使它是一阵一阵地袭来，我和我的焦虑——这位老朋友，我们认识很久了。

sentences.en: I remember distinctly, so clearly, having my first ever panic attack about the movie The NeverEnding Story when I was eight years old at like a school movie night.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得，八岁那年，在学校的电影之夜看《大魔域》时，我第一次经历了恐慌发作。

sentences.en: And since then,
sentences.zh: 从那时起，

sentences.en: I've always had these moments of just extreme panic and anxiety that can go on for months or will just be this baseline of just nervousness for kind of as long as I can remember.
sentences.zh: 我就一直会有那种极度恐慌和焦虑的时刻，有时会持续数月，或者在我记忆所及的范围内，一直处于一种基础的紧张状态。

sentences.en: I think I said in a recent episode that there have even, you know, been times in my life when I've worried about the fact that I'm not anxious about anything,
sentences.zh: 我想我在最近的一期节目中说过，甚至有那么一段时间，我因为自己对任何事情都不感到焦虑而感到担忧，

sentences.en: which is absolutely bizarre.
sentences.zh: 这简直太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I really begun to, you know, realize that my anxiety was almost comforting in a strange way.
sentences.zh: 我真的开始意识到，从某种奇怪的角度来看，我的焦虑甚至让我感到一种慰藉。

sentences.en: It provided me with an illusion of security that felt quite nice when actually, although it was making me feel nice, was making me feel like I could anticipate every single problem
sentences.zh: 它给了我一种虚假的安全感，感觉还不错，但实际上，虽然它让我感觉良好，却让我觉得我能预见到生活中的每一个问题，

sentences.en: that would happen in my life.
sentences.zh: 那些可能会发生的问题。

sentences.en: A, that wasn't the case.
sentences.zh: 首先，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Things happened that I never could have thought of.
sentences.zh: 有些事情发生了，是我从未想到的。

sentences.en: And B, it was actually taking away from a lot of my experiences and a lot of the joyful experiences that made up for the anxious ones.
sentences.zh: 其次，它实际上剥夺了我许多体验，以及许多能够抵消焦虑感的快乐体验。

sentences.en: You know, I would just sit with my anxious thoughts and try and problem solve them, which I think is something that we've all done.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我过去常常坐在那里，带着焦虑的想法试图去解决它们，我想这是我们所有人都做过的事情。

sentences.en: I would try and think my way through a scenario that, you know, is completely irrational and that is just never going to work because even when on the rare occasion
sentences.zh: 我会试图通过思考来解决一个完全不合理的情境，但这永远不会奏效，因为即使在极少数情况下，

sentences.en: I would get through it, my brain would just present me with a bigger and even trickier hypothetical.
sentences.zh: 我解决了问题，我的大脑又会抛给我一个更大、更棘手的假设性难题。

sentences.en: So it felt quite never ending.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉就像永无止境一样。

sentences.en: And then a few years back, I started doing things differently.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我开始尝试不同的做法。

sentences.en: I stopped letting my anxiety kind of be the loudest voice in the room.
sentences.zh: 我不再让焦虑成为房间里最响亮的声音。

sentences.en: I stopped letting it, you know, always be in control.
sentences.zh: 我不再让它总是处于掌控地位。

sentences.en: And I kind of started finding ways to almost play with my anxious thoughts, to like beat them at their own game, combining what I knew scientifically
sentences.zh: 我开始寻找一些方法，几乎是去和我的焦虑想法玩游戏，去以其人之道还治其人之身，结合我所了解的关于焦虑及其运作方式的科学和心理学知识，

sentences.en: and psychologically about anxiety and how it operates, but also by kind of playing these mind games, these mind tricks, and establishing like some pretty
sentences.zh: 同时也通过玩这些心理游戏、心理技巧，并在不断的试错中，建立起一些非常、非常实用的技巧、建议和策略。

sentences.en: really, really useful tricks and tips and strategies through trial and error.
sentences.zh: 而那些真正让我感觉好起来的方法确实需要付出一点努力，但它确实帮助我改变了思维方式，将焦虑从一种负担转变为我的一部分，

sentences.en: And what actually made me feel better did require a little bit of work, but it really helped me change my thinking from anxiety as a burden to anxiety as something
sentences.zh: 我可以让它为我所用，在某种程度上加以利用。

sentences.en: that is a part of me that I can make work for me, that I can leverage in some small way.
sentences.zh: 这正是我想在今天讨论的内容。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what I want to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 我真正能够让焦虑为我所用的四种方法，即使是在非常、非常艰难的时刻，在糟糕、极度恐慌和焦虑的时刻。

sentences.en: Four of the ways that I've really been able to make anxiety work for me, even in really, really tough times, terrible times, really panicky, anxious times.
sentences.zh: 这些策略一直是我最强大的工具。

sentences.en: These strategies have been like my greatest tools.
sentences.zh: 最近，我不得不再次对它们进行测试。

sentences.en: And recently, I really had to put them to the test again.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，它们确实帮助我走出了困境。

sentences.en: And slowly but surely, they have helped me out of a tough situation.
sentences.zh: 所以我很想与你们分享。

sentences.en: So I wanted to share it with you.
sentences.zh: 希望你们能从中有所收获。

sentences.en: I hope that you can learn something.
sentences.zh: 所有这些建议都非常实用且易于上手。

sentences.en: All of these tips are really practical and accessible.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，今天就可以尝试一下。

sentences.en: You could literally try them all today if you wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望，即使它不能改变你的人生，至少也能改变你对焦虑想法的看法。

sentences.en: So I really hope it at least changes how you think about your anxious thoughts, even if it doesn't change your life.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入让焦虑为我们所用的四种方法。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into the four ways that we can make anxiety work for us.
sentences.zh: 重温一下焦虑到底是什么，听起来可能很简单。

sentences.en: Having a refresher on what anxiety actually is might sound really simple to begin with.
sentences.zh: 但有时当我们深陷恐惧、恐慌和担忧之中时，我们会认为焦虑的意义远不止于此。

sentences.en: But sometimes when we're really wrapped up in our fear and our panic and our worry, we think that our anxiety means more than it does.
sentences.zh: 我们首先需要立足于事实，立足于我们所经历的事情的真相。

sentences.en: And we really need to be, firstly, grounded in the fact, grounded in the facts of what we're going through.
sentences.zh: 你可能认为自己了解关于焦虑的所有信息。

sentences.en: You may think you know all the information about anxiety.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多东西需要了解。

sentences.en: There is a lot to know.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能确实了解不少。

sentences.en: And you probably do know quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 但当你处于生存模式和纯粹的恐惧中时，你真正记住这些宝贵信息的能力就会变得相当模糊。

sentences.en: But when you're operating from a place of survival and pure fear, your ability to actually remember this valuable information becomes quite clouded.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的思维不再清晰了。

sentences.en: You know, you're just not thinking straight.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我们认为焦虑比实际情况要严重得多。

sentences.en: And we think in those moments that our anxiety is much more valid than it is.
sentences.zh: 我们认为应该相信脑海中闪过的每一个念头，认为每一个虚构的情境都可能是真的。

sentences.en: That we should believe every single thought that passes through our brains, that every opinion made up situation could be true.
sentences.zh: 因为我们天生倾向于优先考虑与生存、恐惧相关的想法，那些带有情感色彩的想法，即使它们实际上并没有那么有用。

sentences.en: Because we've been hardwired to prioritise thoughts that relate to our survival, that relate to fear, that have an emotional tone to them, even if they're actually not that useful.
sentences.zh: 我想，我们本质上相信，在某种程度上，我们的大脑和身体一定是在做它认为最好的事情。

sentences.en: We, I think, essentially trust that our mind and our body, and to a certain extent, must be doing what it thinks is beSt.
sentences.zh: 它一定知道什么是最好的。

sentences.en: It must know what's beSt.
sentences.zh: 它一定是因为我们处于真正的危险之中，才让我们关注这些假设性的问题。

sentences.en: It must be making us pay attention to these hypotheticals because we are in real danger.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要意识到，我们的信任放错了地方，因为焦虑的工作——这可能会让你感到震惊，也可能不会——焦虑的工作就是不理性。

sentences.en: But what we need to realise is that our trust is misplaced because anxiety's job, and this might shock you, maybe it won't, but anxiety's job is to be irrational.
sentences.zh: 这确实是它的工作。

sentences.en: That is literally its job.
sentences.zh: 它要向我们展示最坏的情况，去灾难化、去施压、去投射，而不是去追求真实。

sentences.en: It is to present us with the worst case scenarios, to catastrophize, to stress, to project, not to be truthful.
sentences.zh: 那不是它工作职责的一部分。

sentences.en: That is not part of its job description.
sentences.zh: 它不是为了现实地看待情况。

sentences.en: It's not to see a situation realistically.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: And why exactly is that the case?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为焦虑是你身体和大脑试图保护你免受感知到的威胁或压力情境的影响，通常是通过夸大结果，

sentences.en: Well, because anxiety is your body and your brain trying to protect you against a perceived threat or a stressful situation, often by exaggerating an outcome
sentences.zh: 或者夸大现实情况，来达到目的，要么是 A，激励你，要么是 B，试图让你在情况发生前解决问题。

sentences.en: or exaggerating the reality of the situation to, you know, either A, help motivate you, or B, try and get you to problem solve before the situation occurs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我经常把焦虑比作大脑试图给你进行一场模拟考试，但所有的题目和情境都是你在现实世界或真正的考试中永远不会遇到的。

sentences.en: You know, I often think about anxiety like your mind trying to give you a practice exam, but all the questions and scenarios are questions and scenarios
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常是无法回答的。

sentences.en: that you'd never actually encounter in the real world or in the real exam.
sentences.zh: 它们永远不会在现实生活中出现。

sentences.en: And they're often impossible to answer.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，你在说服自己，或者你的焦虑在说服你，这不是一场模拟考试。

sentences.en: They'll never show up in real life.
sentences.zh: 这是真的。

sentences.en: And all the while, you're convincing yourself or your anxiety is convincing you, you know, this isn't a practice exam.
sentences.zh: 你必须认真对待。

sentences.en: This is the real deal.
sentences.zh: 这可能现在就在发生。

sentences.en: You have to take this seriously.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，以对未来的焦虑感为例。

sentences.en: This could actually be happening right now.
sentences.zh: 你真正经历的是对不确定性的恐惧，因为有很多事情你不知道。

sentences.en: Now, you know, take feeling anxious about the future.
sentences.zh: 你可能不知道你的职业生涯会如何发展。

sentences.en: What you're really experiencing is a fear of uncertainty because there is a lot you don't know.
sentences.zh: 你可能不知道那个巨大的冒险是否会有回报，你是否会遇到属于你的人，是否会找到真爱。

sentences.en: You might not know how your career is going to turn out.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多空白空间。

sentences.en: You might not know whether that big risk will pay off, whether you're going to meet your people, whether you're going to find love.
sentences.zh: 有很多未知数。

sentences.en: So there is a lot of empty space.
sentences.zh: 我们的焦虑喜欢用最坏的情况来填补这些空间，基本上是说，好吧，如果你能处理好这个，如果你有一个计划，那么如果它真的发生了，我们也会没事的。

sentences.en: There are a lot of unknowns.
sentences.zh: 但问题是。

sentences.en: Our anxiety likes to fill that space with the worst case scenario to basically say, okay, well, if you can handle this, if you have a plan, then we'll be fine if it comes true.
sentences.zh: 这些情境很少，甚至几乎从未发生过。

sentences.en: Here's the thing though.
sentences.zh: 那种你在火灾中失去一切、在工作中犯了大错、再也找不到工作、所有亲人都去世的情境，是不会发生的。

sentences.en: Those scenarios rarely, if not ever, come true.
sentences.zh: 那种突然被诊断出患有罕见疾病的恐惧，而你本来很健康，那也是不会发生的。

sentences.en: The scenario in which you lose everything in a fire and you make a huge mistake at work and you never get a job again and all your loved ones die, that isn't going to come true.
sentences.zh: 或者，你认为每个人都暗中讨厌你，你不知怎么说错了话惹恼了所有亲密朋友，而没有人提起过，那是假的。

sentences.en: The fear of, you know, suddenly being diagnosed with a rare disease when you were otherwise healthy, that isn't going to come true.
sentences.zh: 它不会成真。

sentences.en: Or, you know, your thought that everyone secretly dislikes you, you've somehow said something to upset all your close friends without anyone mentioning it, that is false.
sentences.zh: 这是你的大脑在为你提供情境，给你进行一次非常剧烈的心理和身体锻炼，这样如果它们真的发生了，你也会没事的，因为你已经提前体验过对这种情况的焦虑了。

sentences.en: It's not going to come true.
sentences.zh: 希望这很有道理。

sentences.en: It is your brain serving you up scenarios to give you a really vigorous mental and physical workout so if they were to happen, you would be okay because you've already experienced
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们开始承认这是我们的大脑试图保护我们，但做得并不好，或者根本没有帮助时，我们就能更清楚地看到自己的处境。

sentences.en: the anxiety towards this situation beforehand.
sentences.zh: 提醒自己关于某种情况的看法仅仅是一种看法，这对我来说一直、一直很有帮助。

sentences.en: Hopefully, that makes a lot of sense to you.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已，不多不少。

sentences.en: I think when we begin to acknowledge that this is our brain trying to protect us but just not doing a very great job or being very helpful at all,
sentences.zh: 我的想法往往缺乏证据，而且无论我怎么努力，我都无法预知未来。

sentences.en: we see our situation a bit more clearly and it has always, always helped me to remind myself that my opinion about a situation is just an opinion.
sentences.zh: 我没有那种罕见的魔法能力。

sentences.en: Nothing more, nothing less.
sentences.zh: 我无法预料事情会如何发展。

sentences.en: There's often very little evidence for what I'm thinking and as much as I try, you know, I can't tell the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只能接受即将发生的一切。

sentences.en: I'm not, I don't have that rare magical ability.
sentences.zh: 当然，这想起来很容易，但当你的焦虑伴随着一系列身体症状时，比如颤抖、心跳加速、呼吸急促、

sentences.en: I cannot anticipate how this will work out.
sentences.zh: 发抖、恶心、出汗，或者那种解离感或不真实感，它会变得更加令人不快，而且我得说，这让它感觉更加迫在眉睫。

sentences.en: So, I just have to be accepting of what comes.
sentences.zh: 尽管那些想法可能不是真的，但你所经历的肯定是真实的，你所经历的身体感受是非常真实的。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, that's very easy to think but when your anxiety is accompanied by a number of physical symptoms like shaking, like a rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath,

sentences.en: that I've really started approaching this tension, these feelings, these thoughts in a way that initially felt so counterintuitive but actually which really, really worked

sentences.en: You kind of have to beat it at its own game and just be as irrational and delusional in your belief that you'll be fine as your anxiety is irrational and delusional

sentences.en: in its belief that the world is falling apart.

sentences.en: You need to be just as persistent as your anxiety is and just as imaginative but the thing is, is that you already know that you can be all those things
sentences.zh: 如果我焦虑的大脑想要编造事情，想要在事情并非威胁时将其标记为威胁，如果我焦虑的大脑想要对我撒谎，那么，我也可以反过来对它撒谎。

sentences.en: because your anxiety is displaying that you have that capability so you can use, you know, the methods that your anxiety is using to scare you to kind of scare it back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这听起来像是在与不共戴天的敌人战斗，但事实是，对吧？

sentences.en: This really brings me to the first way that I've stopped fighting my anxiety and really made it work for me and that is really tricking myself into believing
sentences.zh: 感到焦虑有一种不同寻常之处，这反而对我们有利。

sentences.en: that anytime I feel anxiety it's actually just excitement and choosing to label the sensations differently to how my mind wants to label them.

sentences.en: If my anxious mind wants to make things up, wants to label things differently as a threat when they're not, if my anxious mind wants to lie to me, well, I can lie right back.
sentences.zh: 哈佛商学院有一篇非常棒的文章，标题是

sentences.en: You know, it sounds like I'm fighting this like, you know, mortal enemy but here's the thing, right?

sentences.en: Like, there's a perk, not so much a perk but something unusual about feeling anxious that works in our favour.

sentences.en: Anxiety and excitement are actually incredibly similar on so many dimensions and they tend to actually activate the same kind of arousal pathways in our body.
sentences.zh: 当你兴奋时，你可能会感到同样焦躁不安、紧张，你会感觉到心率加快，也许所有这些想法开始涌现，

sentences.zh: 关于什么是可能的。

sentences.zh: 关于什么是可能的。

sentences.en: They're based on high levels of arousal, so basically meaning a similar level of bodily response to a stimulus and they're based on a sense or a loss of control.
sentences.zh: 关于什么是可能的。

sentences.en: When you're excited, you're going to feel perhaps equally jittery, kind of nervous, you're going to feel your heart rate go up, maybe all these thoughts start swirling around
sentences.zh: 关于什么是可能的。

sentences.en: about what is possible.
sentences.zh: 关于什么是可能的。

sentences.en: That's very similar to an anxious state.
sentences.zh: 这与焦虑状态非常相似。

sentences.en: The only difference is what we would call positive or negative valence.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别在于我们所说的正效价或负效价。

sentences.en: So valence or valency is this idea in psychology that describes how different emotions have a different emotional effect, even if they feel the same on a physical level.
sentences.zh: 效价（valence）是心理学中的一个概念，用来描述不同的情绪即使在生理层面感觉相同，也会产生不同的情感影响。

sentences.en: So anxiety and excitement, they feel the same on a physical level, but anxiety has a negative valence, whereas excitement has a positive valence, meaning that the emotional effect
sentences.zh: 焦虑和兴奋在生理层面上的感觉是一样的，但焦虑具有负效价，而兴奋具有正效价，这意味着

sentences.en: of excitement is appealing, it's desirable, it makes us more attracted to a situation, whereas anxiety has that negative valence, it makes us scared, fearful, uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 兴奋的情感影响是吸引人的、令人向往的，它让我们更倾向于某种情境；而焦虑具有负效价，它让我们感到害怕、恐惧和不适。

sentences.en: So I want you to tap into that positive emotional valency.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你能利用那种积极的情感效价。

sentences.en: If the only thing that is different is how we interpret a feeling, then tell yourself, actually, I'm excited by this feeling.
sentences.zh: 如果唯一的区别在于我们如何解读这种感觉，那就告诉自己：其实，我对这种感觉感到兴奋。

sentences.en: I'm excited to see how I manage this.

sentences.en: I'm excited to be able to have this human experience.

sentences.en: The easiest way to tell if something is an anxious thought is when it starts with what if.
sentences.zh: 判断一个想法是否为焦虑想法，最简单的方法就是看它是否以“万一……”开头。

sentences.en: What if the world collapses?
sentences.zh: 万一世界崩溃了怎么办？

sentences.en: What if my worst fear comes true?
sentences.zh: 万一我最害怕的事情成真了怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I never achieve what I want?
sentences.zh: 万一我永远无法实现我想要的怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I lose it all?
sentences.zh: 万一我失去了一切怎么办？

sentences.en: A true fear, something that is actually dangerous in the moment, wouldn't require that what if prefix because you would know it was happening.
sentences.zh: 真正的恐惧，即当下确实危险的事情，不需要“万一”这个前缀，因为你会知道它正在发生。

sentences.en: It would be happening right now in the moment.
sentences.zh: 它会就在当下发生。

sentences.en: And this is really valuable to pay attention to because the moment you find yourself spiraling, overthinking, getting repetitive with your thoughts, and they all start with
sentences.zh: 关注这一点非常有价值，因为当你发现自己陷入恶性循环、过度思考、想法变得重复，并且它们都以

sentences.en: what if, that is anxiety.
sentences.zh: “万一”开头时，那就是焦虑。

sentences.en: That is not reality.
sentences.zh: 那不是现实。

sentences.en: It's a thought, not a fact.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个想法，不是事实。

sentences.en: Here's how you can make this work for you.
sentences.zh: 以下是如何让它为你所用。

sentences.en: Again, what you're really fearing here is the unknown.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，你在这里真正恐惧的是未知。

sentences.en: And it's not uncommon for us to have, you know, five, six, seven different hypotheticals about what could happen all going at once, all swirling around, all feeling equally scary
sentences.zh: 我们同时有五、六、七种关于可能发生什么的假设，它们同时涌现、盘旋，感觉同样可怕

sentences.en: and unlikely.
sentences.zh: 且不太可能发生，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: What we forget to realize is that they can't all possibly come true.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记意识到的是，它们不可能全部成真。

sentences.en: But yet, we feel bombarded with an almost cumulative worry, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们还是感到被一种近乎累积的担忧所轰炸，对吧？

sentences.en: That each of these hypotheticals could be a possibility.
sentences.zh: 认为每一个假设都可能成为现实。

sentences.en: And that's one of the first ways that we see that anxiety is really, really irrational because that's not possible.
sentences.zh: 这是我们看到焦虑非常、非常不理性的第一种方式，因为那是不可能的。

sentences.en: And I want you to fight these unknowns with knowns.
sentences.zh: 我希望你用已知的事实来对抗这些未知。

sentences.en: Yes, you don't know how the future will pan out or what will happen in this situation.
sentences.zh: 是的，你不知道未来会怎样，也不知道在这种情况下会发生什么。

sentences.en: But you do know a lot of things and you are certain of a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 但你确实知道很多事情，并且对很多事情很确定。

sentences.en: You know that you are capable.
sentences.zh: 你知道自己是有能力的。

sentences.en: You know that you've survived every situation you've been in before.
sentences.zh: 你知道你之前经历过的每一种情况都挺过来了。

sentences.en: You know that this is just anxiety.
sentences.zh: 你知道这只是焦虑。

sentences.en: What else do you know?
sentences.zh: 你还知道什么？

sentences.en: You do know that your fears rarely ever come true.
sentences.zh: 你确实知道你的恐惧很少成真。

sentences.en: You do know that you are not alone.
sentences.zh: 你确实知道你并不孤单。

sentences.en: You do know that many others have been through this and come out the other side.
sentences.zh: 你确实知道许多其他人也经历过这些并走了出来。

sentences.en: There is one uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 确实存在一个不确定性。

sentences.en: The uncertainty is what's going to happen in this situation, what's going to happen next.
sentences.zh: 不确定性是这种情况会发生什么，接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: But there are many, many certainties.
sentences.zh: 但有很多、很多的确定性。

sentences.en: And that is what I want you to focus on.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我想让你关注的地方。

sentences.en: What you do know, what you are certain of compared to what you are uncertain of and see how the certainties end up stacking up in your favor.
sentences.zh: 关注你知道的、你确定的事情，对比你不确定的事情，看看这些确定性如何最终堆叠起来，对你有利。

sentences.en: Here's a really great visualization exercise that I use with this as well is I like pretend that I am holding these certainties in my hand and they are these big golden orbs,
sentences.zh: 这里有一个非常棒的可视化练习，我也经常用它。我喜欢假装我手里拿着这些确定性，它们是巨大的金色球体，

sentences.en: these big like weird golden balls and I like mentally throw them at my fears, at my anxious thoughts and I think about the fears as like this big shadowy, you know, shadowy figure
sentences.zh: 这些巨大的、奇怪的金色球体。我在脑海中把它们扔向我的恐惧，扔向我的焦虑想法。我把恐惧想象成一个巨大的阴影，你知道，阴影人物，

sentences.en: and I'm throwing these big certainty golden orbs at them and they're just crashing through this shadow making it smaller and smaller and smaller making it fall apart
sentences.zh: 我把这些巨大的确定性金球扔向它们，它们撞碎了阴影，让它变得越来越小，直到它分崩离析，

sentences.en: until it's gone and these certainties really pierce through that uncertainty both in like the visualization but also in your life like you really start to believe that yes,
sentences.zh: 直到它消失。这些确定性确实刺穿了那种不确定性，不仅是在可视化中，在你的生活中也是如此。你真的开始相信，是的，

sentences.en: you know, you do know that this is going to pass.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你确实知道这一切都会过去。

sentences.en: You do know that there are all these factual things that you can rely on.
sentences.zh: 你确实知道有所有这些你可以依赖的事实。

sentences.en: You do know at the very least that you trust yourself to get through this.
sentences.zh: 你至少知道你相信自己能度过难关。

sentences.en: That is something that you are absolutely sure of.
sentences.zh: 这是你绝对确定的事情。

sentences.en: The reason that I find this so effective is because it gives me the opportunity to remember that I am capable no matter what situation I encounter.
sentences.zh: 我发现这个方法如此有效的原因是，它让我有机会记住，无论遇到什么情况，我都有能力应对。

sentences.en: Again, anxiety's job is to be irrational but so often afterwards we never get the opportunity to remember what it was we were fearing because it doesn't come true.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，焦虑的工作是不理性的，但事后我们往往没有机会记住我们害怕的是什么，因为它并没有成真。

sentences.en: So anxiety's job is really to torment us not to give us factual scenarios that we actually are going to encounter.
sentences.zh: 所以焦虑的工作确实是折磨我们，而不是给我们提供我们真正会遇到的事实场景。

sentences.en: You can instead use this situation to learn about yourself to reinforce that you are confident that you trust yourself rather than trusting your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 相反，你可以利用这种情况来了解自己，加强你的自信，相信自己，而不是相信你的焦虑。

sentences.en: And you've got to remember a lot of people don't get tested this way.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，很多人并没有经历过这种考验。

sentences.en: A lot of people go through life just assuming things and you're someone who is going to instead take that discomfort, take all those situations in which you felt fear
sentences.zh: 很多人一生都在假设中度过，而你是一个愿意接受这种不适，接受所有让你感到恐惧的情况的人，

sentences.en: and really pay attention to the fact that you got through it.
sentences.zh: 并真正关注你挺过来的事实。

sentences.en: And really remember that for the future that you are an incredibly strong person to be facing a battle that is originating from you that is originating from the deepest fears
sentences.zh: 并真正为未来记住这一点：你是一个极其坚强的人，正在面对一场源于你自身的战斗，一场源于你可能遇到的最深层恐惧的战斗，

sentences.en: that you could possibly encounter being made to feel real.
sentences.zh: 并让它们感觉真实。

sentences.en: I just think you will experience true pride and joy that you persevered and I want you to have that experience and I want you to make that happen for yourself.
